pretreatments.description: Electrohydrolysis pretreatment: Application of DC current with varying voltage (up to 15 V) and time (up to 45 min) to the PPMS slurry, utilizing a flash mixer at 300 rpm, resulting in particle disintegration, microbial cell lysis, ohmic heating, electrophoresis, and solubilization of organic matter.
Cow dung inoculum: Use of cow dung collected from a farm as an inoculum for the batch anaerobic digestion study.
Slurry preparation: Preparation of a PPMS slurry by mixing the solid PPMS with distilled water in a 1:3 ratio to facilitate the electrohydrolysis process and prevent clogging.

Batch anaerobic biodegradability tests: Performance of batch anaerobic biodegradability tests using a fixed food to microorganisms ratio (2:1) and maintaining the reactor at room temperature (30-38 °C) with manual mixing three to four times daily.
Nutrient addition: Addition of essential macro and micro nutrients to the anaerobic reactors.
Nitrogen purging: Purging of the anaerobic reactors with nitrogen to create an anaerobic environment.

CO2 and H2S absorption: Coupling of the anaerobic reactors with an aspirator bottle containing 1.5 N NaOH solution to absorb CO2 and H2S and displace NaOH solution, representing methane (CH4) production.
Control experiment: Use of untreated PPMS as a control sample for comparison with the electrohydrolysis pretreated PPMS.
